the effect of the angle at which the infrared beam is incident on the steel surface (θi) on the band intensities and band positions in the spectra of corroded steel is dependent on the level of surface roughness of the steel surface.

the angle of incidence has a significant effect on the band intensities and the number of observed bands of the far-infrared spectra of carbon steel corroded at 80 °C in CO2-saturate brine, in the presence and in the absence of the corrosion inhibitors 2-mercapto-5-nitro-1,3,4-thiadiazole and 2-meraptopyrimidine.

the use of variable θi can provide additional information to the spectra of rough surfaces, which can be useful in the identification of corrosion products and in the determination of the surface roughness.
